client: python-httpx language-neutral probe (not a native client)
environment: local lane Supabase stack argus-native-auth-proof (jwt_expiry=60, confirmations on) + unchanged Argus API; Argus API launched from the fix branch at argus_api_head

results.expected: Confirmation returns to the web site_url; Argus signup has no redirect parameter a native client could set
results.note: Hosted: lands on the web app with an implicit-flow session in the URL fragment. A native return needs Argus to pass emailRedirectTo (proposal P4).

results.scenario: PKCE recovery that returns to an allowlisted app callback
results.expected: Link redirects to the app scheme with ?code; exchange with the verifier yields a session Argus accepts

results.scenario: The same callback delivered twice, and the same email link opened twice
results.expected: Second exchange refused; second link open returns an error to the callback, not a code

results.scenario: A code arrives on a device that did not start the flow (wrong verifier), and a forged code
results.note: PKCE binds the link to the device that requested it. A user who requests recovery on the phone and opens the email on a laptop cannot finish on the laptop through this flow.

results.scenario: Recovery requested with a redirect that is not on the allowlist
results.expected: Supabase ignores the unlisted redirect and falls back to site_url

results.scenario: Password reset by recovery, then sign out everywhere as the web recovery page does
results.expected: Other sessions end after the reset; the recovery session ends after signOut(scope: global)
results.note: Supabase revoked the other session on the password update itself. Native recovery still ends with a global sign-out, matching web/lib/auth-security.ts resetRecoveredPassword, so the recovery session does not linger.

results.scenario: Recovery link opened after otp_expiry (60 s on the lane stack)
results.expected: Callback receives an error, not a code
